turns.en: That's not really a very apt comparison. Oh, and so sorry, you asked the question about how close the matches look. It's not that close. P, every quarter, they just get to decide what the numbers are for the quarter.
turns.zh: 那不是个很贴切的比较。哦，抱歉，你之前问过匹配得有多接近的问题。其实没那么接近。PE 每个季度可以自己决定那个季度的数字是多少。

turns.en: And so over time, yes, it's a similar risk and return pattern. In other words, the volatility level, like downside vol of this kind of strategy, I believe has been and I believe it could easily be similar in the future to what we see in private equity and average returns.
turns.zh: 所以从长期看，是的，风险-收益形态是相似的。换句话说，这种策略的下行波动率，我相信过去与私募股权所见的水平相似，将来也很容易做到相似，平均收益也一样。

turns.en: I think historically on a post fee basis have been comparable to average private equity, not top quartile private equity. And so again, if you were a genius who could pick top quartile funds, do that by all means for them, we just want to be a tool in the toolbox to help the managers there portfolio better.
turns.zh: 我觉得从历史上看，在扣除费用之后，它与平均水平的私募股权可比，而不是顶尖四分位的私募股权。所以再说一次，如果你是有本事挑中顶尖四分位基金的天才，尽管去那么做——对我们而言，我们只想做工具箱里的一个工具，帮那些管理人把组合做得更好。

turns.en: But it is quarter by quarter, you're not going to match that closely. The key is to say when the market's up a lot and he's up, you want to be up also.
turns.zh: 但要说每个季度都对得上，你不可能匹配得那么紧。关键在于：当市场大涨、PE 也涨的时候，你也想跟着涨。

turns.en: And when the market crashes and he protects you some from the crash, you want to protect that. And those are the most important things. And if there's a quarter where he's up three and you're down to or vice versa, as long as those average out to where the performance is similar, that's not something that I think people should sweat too much because it's just not realistic to match those numbers, which essentially come
turns.zh: 而当市场崩盘、PE 多少保护了你一点的时候，你也想把那份保护做到。这些是最重要的东西。如果某个季度它涨 3、你跌 2，或者反过来，只要这些在业绩上摊平后大体相似，那我觉得人们不必太纠结，因为要匹配那些数字本来就不现实——那些数字说到底

turns.en: out of people's heads as opposed to coming out of market prices. Last little topic we touched on the top seven or 10 in the S&P. It's an AI trade.
turns.zh: 是来自别人脑子里定的，而不是来自市场价格。——好，最后一个我们之前碰过的小话题，就是标普的前七或前十。这是一个关于 AI 的交易。

turns.en: What does AI and these new large language models tools, the tools that they provide, what does it mean for academic research and finance? How are you using them?
turns.zh: AI 和这些新的大语言模型工具、它们提供的工具，对金融领域的学术研究意味着什么？你是怎么使用它们的？

turns.en: What are you excited about? Yeah, it is. You know, I was thinking about this with a guy I was just with my colleague, Lauren Cohen, no relation, amazing scholar and amazing human being.
turns.zh: 你对什么感到兴奋？——是啊，确实。你知道，我最近和一个人聊了这个——我刚和我的同事 Lauren Cohen 在一起，我们并无亲属关系——他是一位了不起的学者，也是一位了不起的人。

turns.en: And Lauren wrote this wonderful paper in the pre-generative AI era. And what he did, he got the risk reports. You know how in the 10Ks, there's a risk factors section in every 10K.
turns.zh: Lauren 在前生成式 AI 时代写过一篇精彩的论文。他做的事是：他拿到风险报告。你知道在 10-K（年报）里，每份 10-K 都有一个风险因素章节。

turns.en: And he pulled these risk factors section and all he did was use old school, relatively simple machine learning to compare to see has anything changed from last year to this year, even one word.
turns.zh: 他把这些风险因素章节抽出来，全部做的只是用老派的、相对简单的机器学习来比较：从上年到今年，有没有哪怕一个字发生变化。

turns.en: If anything changed, obviously, you know, you might hand check it to make sure it's not just that they misplaced the comma, but fundamentally to the risk statement change.
turns.zh: 如果有变化，显然你可以人工检查一下，确认那不过是逗号放错了位置之类——但从根本上讲，风险陈述有没有变。

turns.en: And then he said, let's identify the small subset. Most years, no change. The small subset that changed from year to year. What happened to the stock afterwards?
turns.zh: 然后他说：我们来识别出那一小部分。大多数年份没有变化。那一小部分从一年到一年发生了变化。之后股价怎么样了？

turns.en: The answer is the stocks got killed. Okay. There was any change in the risk statement in any direction, then on average, it was, and you can see what's going on here.
turns.zh: 答案是：股价被砸惨了。好，只要风险陈述有任何变化，不管朝哪个方向，平均而言股价都——你能看出这里发生了什么。

turns.en: The lawyers are saying every year you're like, let's not make any change. So the risk statement, right? We've got all the risk started. Finally, we don't want to change it.
turns.zh: 律师们每年都在说：我们别做任何改动，对吧，风险陈述——我们都把风险列好了，不想动它。

turns.en: And if you change it, it's because there is something scary coming down the pike doesn't mean it's going to hit, but it is such a big risk that the lawyers say you got to change it.
turns.zh: 而如果你动了它，那是因为有什么可怕的东西正逼近——不一定是它会砸下来——但那是个足够大的风险，律师说你必须改。

turns.en: So those companies on average did not have good outcomes. All right. And so that was a beautiful paper written with pre AI technology.
